item.title: Fireworks await fans
item.description: FOOTBALL fans can expect two exciting encounters when the semi-finals of the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants are played at Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba tomorrow. Group A winner Global Care Suva FC will face hosts Dayals Steel Ba FC in the opening semi-final at 2pm, before Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC takes on Nasinu FC at 4.30pm.
item.content:encoded:
FOOTBALL fans can expect two exciting encounters when the semi-finals of the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants are played at Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba tomorrow.

Group A winner Global Care Suva FC will face hosts Dayals Steel Ba FC in the opening semi-final at 2pm, before Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC takes on Nasinu FC at 4.30pm.

Fiji Football Association CEO Mohammed Yusuf said the four teams had earned their places in the knockout stage after an exciting three days of pool competition.

“We witnessed three days of competitive football during the pool stage, and the four best teams have qualified for the semi-finals.

“Fans can expect two thrilling matches because every team will be fighting for a place in the final.

“We encourage football supporters from around the country to come to Ba with their families and enjoy another exciting weekend of football,” Yusuf said.

Suva enters the knockout stage after recording impressive victories over Blue Gas Navua FC and defending champion Extra Supermarket Labasa FC.

Coach Pita Rabo’s side scored seven goals in its three pool matches and will now face a determined Ba side in front of its home supporters.

The Men in Black secured their semi-final berth with victories over Tagimoucia Kava Nadi FC and Khelvin Engineering Lautoka FC.

Under coach Ravinesh Kumar, Ba has already won the BiC Fiji FACT and Extra Premier League titles this season and remains in contention for a third major trophy.

The second semi-final promises another intriguing contest, with nine-time champion Rewa facing tournament surprise package Nasinu. Rewa topped Group B after convincing victories over Lautoka and Ba. The Delta Tigers will be eager to bounce back after suffering a narrow 0-1 defeat to Nadi in their final pool match.

Nasinu has been one of the tournament’s surprise packages, recovering from an opening loss to Labasa to register consecutive victories over Navua and Suva.

The Giant Killers will feature in their first BOG semi-final since 2019. With defending champion Labasa eliminated during the pool stage, a new champion will be crowned this year.

The winners of tomorrow’s semi-finals will meet in the grand final at 3pm on Sunday.

Dayal’s Steel Ba’s Nabil Begg in action against Khelvin Realtors Lautoka during their match in the Extra Battle of the Giants tournament held at 4R Stadium in Govind Park Ba on 6th September 2026. Picture: REINAL CHAND

item.title: Rewa FC side wary of Nasinu
item.description: STRATUM/PPCL Rewa FC will be aiming to move a step closer to claiming its 10th Battle of the Giants title when it takes on Nasinu FC in the second semi-final tomorrow. The Delta Tigers topped Group B after securing six points from their three pool matches at Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.
item.content:encoded:
STRATUM/PPCL Rewa FC will be aiming to move a step closer to claiming its 10th Battle of the Giants title when it takes on Nasinu FC in the second semi-final tomorrow.

The Delta Tigers topped Group B after securing six points from their three pool matches at Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.

Rewa opened its campaign with a 2-0 victory over Khelvin Engineering Lautoka FC before producing a dominant display to defeat hosts Dayal’s Steel Ba FC 3-0.

Despite going down 0-1 to Tagimoucia Kava Nadi FC in its final pool match, Rewa had already done enough to secure top spot and book its place in the semi-finals.

Player-coach Ratu Tevita Waranivalu will be expecting an improved performance from his players when they face a determined Nasinu side.

Rewa enters the knockout stage with plenty of experience in its squad, with several players having featured in the OFC Men’s Champions League earlier this season, where the Delta Tigers reached the semi-finals.

The side will also draw confidence from its strong domestic campaign, finishing third in the Extra Premier League.

Nasinu, however, is expected to provide a stern challenge after qualifying for its first BOG semi-final since 2019.

The Giant Killers bounced back from an opening defeat to Extra Supermarket Labasa FC by recording consecutive victories over Blue Gas Navua FC and Global Care Suva FC.

Rewa, which has won the BOG title nine times, will be determined to add another championship to its proud history.

The second semi-final between Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC and Nasinu FC kicks off at 4.30pm tomorrow at Four R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.

item.title: Lomani ready for THE challenge
item.description: VODAFONE Fijiana XV captain Kolora Lomani is looking forward to testing Fiji’s strength against some of the world’s best women’s rugby teams in the inaugural WXV Global Series Challenger in Hong Kong. The Fijiana arrived in Hong Kong ahead of the three-week tournament, which brings together Fiji, Hong Kong China, the Netherlands, Samoa, Spain and Brazil at the Kai Tak Youth Sports Ground.
item.content:encoded:
VODAFONE Fijiana XV captain Kolora Lomani is looking forward to testing Fiji’s strength against some of the world’s best women’s rugby teams in the inaugural WXV Global Series Challenger in Hong Kong.

The Fijiana arrived in Hong Kong ahead of the three-week tournament, which brings together Fiji, Hong Kong China, the Netherlands, Samoa, Spain and Brazil at the Kai Tak Youth Sports Ground.

Fiji will open its campaign against Spain on Sunday, with Lomani expecting a tough contest against a side she knows well.

“We played against Spain in Dubai in the last WXV.

“They’re very physical and a strong team. We’re really excited for the challenge,” Lomani said.

The Fijiana will then face Hong Kong China on September 19 before completing their campaign against the Netherlands on September 26.

The tournament will feature nine international matches over three weekends, with three matches played on each match day.

For Fiji, the series provides an important opportunity to gain valuable international exposure and build momentum towards the next Women’s Rugby World Cup cycle.

The centrally hosted WXV Global Series Challenger is part of World Rugby’s evolving WXV Global Series, designed to provide more competitive matches for women’s teams while building towards the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2029.

Fiji is among 13 teams still competing for the remaining 11 places at the 2029 World Cup.

Five teams have already secured qualification, with hosts Australia joining the top four teams from the last World Cup champions England, Canada, New Zealand and France.

Eight of the remaining places will be decided through 2027 regional competitions, while two will go to the highest-ranked non-qualified teams in the World Rugby Women’s Rankings at the end of the 2027 international window.

The final place will be decided through the WXV Global Series Challenger in 2028.

item.title: Hard work, junior pathway drive Nadera’s finals charge
item.description: HARD work and a strong junior pathway have put Dee Cee’s Nadera Panthers within touching distance of a successful finish to their national rugby league campaign. Founded in 1992, the Nadera club has continued to underline its strength across the grades, with all five teams advancing to the national knockout stages this Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
HARD work and a strong junior pathway have put Dee Cee’s Nadera Panthers within touching distance of a successful finish to their national rugby league campaign.

Founded in 1992, the Nadera club has continued to underline its strength across the grades, with all five teams advancing to the national knockout stages this Saturday.

Coach Vula Dakuitoga believes that achievement is no coincidence.

“There’s nothing sinister about it. It’s just pure hard work,” Dakuitoga said.

The Panthers’ depth will be tested across three venues, with the U13 side facing Veiyasana Knights at Buckhurst Ground, while the U17s meet Makoi Bulldogs and the U19s take on USP Raiders at the same venue.

At Bidesi Ground, the U15 side faces Bukoi Bulldogs in the semi-final.

The Premier grade will then bring the Panthers’ campaign to the main stage at Buckhurst Ground when they meet Namuaniwaqa Sea Eagles in the final match of the day.

For Dakuitoga, the presence of all five teams at this stage reflects the work being done well before players reach the senior grades.

Training is organised across the junior teams, beginning with the U13s before progressing through the U15, U17 and U19 grades.

“We work really hard in terms of conditioning, the physical side of things, especially teaching the boys the real basics of rugby league,” he said.

Dakuitoga said the junior program had also brought another important element to the club — family support.

“When the juniors come, the whole family comes around,” he said.

That support has helped create a strong following around the Panthers while giving younger players a pathway to senior rugby league.

The system has also produced players now pushing for national honours.

Nadera has two players in the Fiji Bati extended squad, halfback Mesake Kurukitoga and forward Haunga Tokona.

Kurukitoga was part of Fiji’s 2022 Rugby League World Cup squad, while Dakuitoga described him as the organiser of the backline and Tokona as a key figure in the forward pack.

With the knockout matches approaching, Dakuitoga wants his players to treat Saturday as another opportunity to improve.

“For me, the team that I wanted to beat next week is Nadera this week,” he said, explaining that the Panthers needed to eliminate the weaknesses they showed the previous week.

That mindset will be central as the Panthers chase success across all five grades.

item.title: Four likely for debut
item.description: THE FIJI Water Flying Fijians will unleash four debutants when they open their Pacific Nations Cup campaign against Canada tomorrow night. Ba native Isoa Tuwai, Penaia Cakobau, Inoke Ravuiwasa and Terio Tamani have been named in the 23-member squad by head coach Senirusi Seruvakula.
item.content:encoded:
THE FIJI Water Flying Fijians will unleash four debutants when they open their Pacific Nations Cup campaign against Canada tomorrow night.

Ba native Isoa Tuwai, Penaia Cakobau, Inoke Ravuiwasa and Terio Tamani have been named in the 23-member squad by head coach Senirusi Seruvakula.

Tuwai will make his debut in the starting XV, while Cakobau, Ravuiwasa and Tamani will provide impact from the bench.

Seruvakula said the team had prepared well for the opening match and was ready for the challenge.

“The team has been preparing well. No injury in the team and everyone is ready to go.

“The four debutants, these players showed potential and they earn the spot.”

Tuwai will man the back of the scrum while Frank Lomani will don the nine jersey as Isaiah Armstrong will slot at first five-eighth.

The backline also features Manasa Mataele, Kalaveti Ravouvou, Virimi Vakatawa, Joji Nasova and Isikeli Rabitu.

Up front, Peni Ravai, Tevita Ikanivere and Mesake Doge will start in the front row, with Mesake Vocevoce and Temo Mayanavanua named in the second row. Kitione Salawa, Motikiai Murray and Tuwai complete the starting forward pack.

The Flying Fijians will be aiming for a strong start to their Pacific Nations Cup campaign against Canada.

Peni Ravai, Tevita Ikanivere, Mesake Doge, Mesake Vocevoce, Temo Mayanavanua, Kitione Salawa, Motikiai Murray, Isoa Tuwai, Frank Lomani, Isaiah Armstrong, Manasa Mataele, Kalaveti Ravouvou, Virimi Vakatawa, Joji Nasova, Isikeli Rabitu.

Reserves: Penaia Cakobau, Meli Tuni, Inoke Ravuiwasa, Isoa Nasilasila, Joseva Tamani, Terio Tamani, Caleb Muntz, Tuidraki Samusamuvodre.

item.title: AIMS Games experience a boost for duo
item.description: FIJI’S young badminton representatives Abigail Corrie of St Anne’s Suva and Arohan Gogoi of Drasa Avenue Lautoka are gaining valuable international experience at the 2026 Zespri AIMS Games School Sporting Championships in Tauranga, New Zealand. The pair completed their singles campaigns on Tuesday after two days of ranking pool matches before moving into the mixed doubles competition yesterday.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI’S young badminton representatives Abigail Corrie of St Anne’s Suva and Arohan Gogoi of Drasa Avenue Lautoka are gaining valuable international experience at the 2026 Zespri AIMS Games School Sporting Championships in Tauranga, New Zealand.

The pair completed their singles campaigns on Tuesday after two days of ranking pool matches before moving into the mixed doubles competition yesterday.

Gogoi secured one victory in his finals division before bowing out after a closely contested second match.

Corrie enjoyed a stronger run, winning three matches before her singles campaign ended in the quarter-finals.

The St Anne’s student finished her singles campaign with a smile despite missing out on a place in the semi-finals.

The mixed doubles competition provided both players with another opportunity to test themselves against young players from across the region.

Their participation at the AIMS Games is part of a growing pathway for young badminton players in Fiji, with the tournament providing exposure to international competition at an early age.

Badminton Fiji president Abel Caine had earlier described Gogoi’s selection as a reflection of the development of badminton at grassroots level in Fiji.

Caine also highlighted the significance of the AIMS Games, which brings together young athletes from New Zealand, Australia and Fiji.

For Gogoi, the tournament marked a significant milestone after he became Drasa Avenue Primary School’s first badminton representative at the AIMS Games.

Corrie also made history for St Anne’s, with the school adding badminton to its participation at the tournament this year.

The two players now return to Fiji with further experience gained from competing on the international school sporting stage.

Their performances in Tauranga also provide an important benchmark as they continue their development in badminton and look towards future opportunities in the sport.

With the singles and mixed doubles competitions now completed, the focus will be on building on the experience gained from their AIMS Games campaign.

For Fiji badminton, the exposure provided to young players such as Corrie and Gogoi is another step towards strengthening the sport’s junior pathway and encouraging greater participation at school level.

item.title: Young Chand ready for Ba semi-finals battle
item.description: FACING players with more experience will be part of the challenge for 17-year-old Abraham Chand when Global Care Suva FC meets Dayals Steel Ba FC in the first semifinal this weekend. The DAV College, Suva student is the youngest player in the Global Care Suva FC squad, but Chand is looking forward to the opportunity to test himself in an important match.
item.content:encoded:
FACING players with more experience will be part of the challenge for 17-year-old Abraham Chand when Global Care Suva FC meets Dayals Steel Ba FC in the first semifinal this weekend.

The DAV College, Suva student is the youngest player in the Global Care Suva FC squad, but Chand is looking forward to the opportunity to test himself in an important match.

For the teenager, reaching the semifinal is something he is proud of after the team secured its place in the final stages of the competition.

“I’m proud of the team that we qualified for the same finals, and we’ll try our best to win,” Chand said.

Chand started playing football at the age of 12 before joining Global Care Suva FC last year when he was 16.

His move to the club has seen him step into an environment where he plays alongside older players, providing him with valuable experience as he continues his football development.

That experience will now be put to the test against Dayals Steel Ba FC, with a place in the final at stake.

For Chand, the age difference between himself and some of his opponents is part of the challenge he has taken on since moving into senior football.

Rather than being intimidated by the occasion, the teenager is focused on giving his best and helping Global Care Suva FC get through the semifinal.

The match will also provide Chand with another opportunity to build his experience at a crucial stage of the competition.

Having started his football journey at 12 and joined Global Care Suva FC at 16, Chand has made steady progress in a short period.

Now, at 17, he faces a new test against Dayals Steel Ba FC, with the young midfielder determined to play his part as Global Care Suva FC pushes for a place in the final.

item.title: Lautoka next test for Suva
item.description: EXPERIENCE will be important for Suva when the side takes on Lautoka in the Subrails Marama Championship at Bidesi Park at 1pm today. The capital side has won its past three matches and will enter today’s clash with confidence after coming from behind to beat Kadavu 19-10 last Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
EXPERIENCE will be important for Suva when the side takes on Lautoka in the Subrails Marama Championship at Bidesi Park at 1pm today.

The capital side has won its past three matches and will enter today’s clash with confidence after coming from behind to beat Kadavu 19-10 last Saturday.

Kadavu led 10-7 at halftime, but Suva produced a stronger second-half performance to secure the victory and continue its push in the competition.

Captain Bulou Wainikiti Vasuturaga said the team was aware of the challenge ahead and needed to continue working on areas that required improvement.

“Every women’s team is powerful,” she said. “We just need to identify our weaknesses clearly, fix them during training, and make sure we’re better in our next game.”

The match will also provide another opportunity for Suva’s younger players to gain valuable experience alongside senior players such as Vasuturaga and Luisa Tisolo.

Head coach Meli Tuifagalele said the experience within the squad had been important in helping develop the younger members of the team.

“They came back to us at the right time. We have a very young squad,” he said.

Suva’s only defeat came against Nadi in round three, a result Tuifagalele said had highlighted the need for his players to remain disciplined and follow the structure developed during training.

The loss has since been followed by three straight victories, including wins over Kadavu and other opponents as Suva regained its momentum.

Lautoka will now provide another test for the side, with Tuifagalele expecting the Western team to adopt an expansive approach.

Suva will need to maintain its structure and make the most of its experience if it is to extend its winning run when the two sides meet today.
